title: Agent reads a ticket for Kim

actors.label: AI agent
actors.description: An MCP client, e.g. a coding assistant

story.title: You asked the agent
story.what: Kim asked the agent to work with ticket 42.
story.why: The agent has no rights of its own here. It acts strictly on Kim's behalf.
story.matters: Every agent action traces back to a real person and inherits that person's limits.

story.title: The gateway brokered the request to the identity provider
story.what: The gateway presented Kim's identity and the agent's own credentials, asking for an Identity Assertion JWT (ID-JAG).
story.why: An agent can't mint its own access. Only the identity provider issues tokens, and only after evaluating policy.
story.matters: The exchange is the checkpoint: every agent action passes through policy before it can touch a resource.

story.title: The identity provider minted a scoped token
story.what: Policy matched Kim, and a token scoped to tickets.read was issued for the ticket API.
story.why: The token is the intersection of what the user may do and what this agent may do.
story.matters: The agent borrows the user's keys, bounded to the user's rights. It can never exceed them.

story.title: The ticket API honored the call
story.what: The API validated the token and returned ticket 42.
story.why: The token carried exactly the scope this call required, and nothing more.
story.matters: Access was proven for this one call, not assumed from a standing login.

subtitle: Cross App Access: ID-JAG token exchange through an MCP gateway

outcome.headline: ✓ ALLOWED: TOKEN ISSUED
outcome.detail: Policy authorized Kim and minted a token for the ticket API, bounded to what Kim may do.
outcome.caption: scoped token minted · API returned 200

tokens.label: Delegated access token
tokens.note: sub is the user; act.sub is the agent acting on their behalf (RFC 8693 actor claim).
